name: Bengaluru
body: Greater Bengaluru Authority and five city corporations

does.text: Streets, solid waste, building rules and property tax.

facts.label: Who runs the city
facts.text: On 2 September 2025 Karnataka notified five city corporations under the Greater Bengaluru Governance Act, 2024, to replace the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP): Bengaluru Central, North, South, East and West. Above them is the Greater Bengaluru Authority, headed by the Chief Minister as ex officio chairperson.

facts.label: Elected council
facts.text: None. The five-year term of the last BBMP council ended in September 2020, and an IAS officer took charge as administrator until new corporators are elected. No election has been held since.

facts.label: Last election
facts.text: Held on 22 August 2015, for 198 wards. The BJP won 100, the Congress 76, the JD(S) 14 and others 8.

facts.label: Next election
facts.text: On 17 July 2026 the Supreme Court directed that elections to all five corporations be held in December 2026. In November 2026 the State Election Commission asked the Court to extend this to 31 January 2027.

facts.label: Wards
facts.text: 369 wards, in the final delimitation notified on 19 November 2025: Central 63, North 72, South 72, East 50, West 112.

facts.label: What a corporation does
facts.text: All functions related to public streets, building bye-laws, disposal of municipal solid waste, and taxes including property tax. Each ward is to have a ward committee chaired by its councillor, to ensure the upkeep of civic services such as solid waste management, sewerage, water supply and street lighting.
